# nonSlide

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a slide.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonSlide() — Checks whether a value is **not** a slide. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/slide</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonSlide<T>(value: T | GoogleAppsScript.Slides.Slide): value is T;
```

`nonSlide(value)` is the same test as `!isSlide(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard looks for the methods that define the type — `getObjectId`, `getPageElementById`. A stub that implements them passes, which is what makes code using this guard testable outside the runtime.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type                                 | Description         |
| :-------- | :----------------------------------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| GoogleAppsScript.Slides.Slide` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a slide; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
const slide = SlidesApp.getActivePresentation().getSlides()[0];

nonSlide({}); // => true
nonSlide(null); // => true
nonSlide(slide); // => false
```
